name: scheduling
deprecation_criterion: Superseded when scheduling moves to a different clock source (e.g. a native plugin cron API) or when the tick interval/route become config-driven and this slice's hardcoding is removed.
spec_change_reason: The /auto-maintainer:start (v0.5.0) and /auto-maintainer:tick (v0.8.0) shipped SKILL.md bodies embed 'config is the bound' operator-in-control guidance: the loop's operational limits are operator-owned (budget.per_day_tokens, backoff.threshold, issue_filter, mode, route/adapter-map) and the deterministic runner enforces them (budget pre-gate, backoff, park, label filter). The executor invents no ad-hoc token/tick/issue caps and does not silently narrow the configured scope; when no limit is configured and the tick signal is refire it keeps draining; subagent_tokens is metered into the configured budget window ONLY (never itself a stop trigger); and a genuine anomaly is surfaced to the operator, who bounds via /auto-maintainer:configure or halts via /auto-maintainer:stop. Framed operator-in-control + anomaly-surfacing, NOT an absolutist never-stop mandate. Additive: the /tick spend-metering steps are unchanged. feature.json advanced 0.50.0 -> 0.51.0.
spec_no_change_reason: spec.md was already advanced to 0.51.0 (config-is-the-bound operator-in-control guidance for the start + tick skills) by the dispatcher's spec-update commit 0c1f5b9 before this TDD cycle; this cycle implements that spec in the two SKILL.md bodies
